searchText: Yeah, fair enough What was the rationale of calling it `EXCHANGE` rather than `SWAPNM`? My google perusal shows that other opcode architectures use the name exchange more than they use swap when having values trade places. mostly register based opcodes however. Not a huge rationale, it was just deemed that SWAP_N_M might be confusing compared to SWAP I think having both swap and exchange is kind of confusing from a vocabulary perspective (they mean essentially the same thing in english) They could be differentiated better with suffixes imo. Maybe SWAP_G (for "swap generic")
